task.description: Gate REQ-228 (entity event registration + create/update/delete record commands, Letflow.EventStore.append_multi/3 refactor, entity_record_latest/entity_type_instances tables) against security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-9, independently re-verifying every claim in handoffs/WF02-REQ228-20260906/step-02-elixir-dev.json rather than trusting it.

result.note:
Scope test: this IS a tenant-data path (new migrations, new schema modules, new command functions touching tenant business data) -- full INV review performed, not skipped.

INV-1 (tenant isolation) -- APPLIES, SATISFIED. Read both migration files directly (priv/repo/migrations/20260906010001_create_entity_record_latest.exs, ...010002_create_entity_type_instances.exs): both wrap table creation in `if prefix() do ... create table(..., prefix: schema) ... end`, matching REQ-226's established schema-per-tenant pattern -- genuinely per-tenant Postgres schemas, not a shared table with a tenant_id predicate that could leak on a forgotten WHERE clause. (a) Every query path confirmed prefix-scoped: EntityTypeInstance.get_or_create/2 uses Repo.get(..., prefix: prefix) and Repo.insert(..., prefix: prefix); Record.Latest's changesets are written via repo.insert/repo.update inside run_command's Multi.run with prefix: ctx.prefix (records.ex lines 286, 297); EventStore.append_multi/3 resolves tenant_id via TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix) and threads schema_name through every M1-M6 step exactly as append/2 already does. (b) Neither table is left reachable in `public` -- both are inside the `if prefix()` guard with no fallback branch. (c) tenant_id is never accepted as a caller-supplied field: Letflow.Entities.Records's create_attrs/update_attrs/delete_attrs types have no tenant_id field at all, and EventStore.append_multi/3 (event_store.ex line 220) calls `reject_tenant_id(attrs)` as the very first `with` clause, identical to append/2's existing P0 check -- a caller-supplied tenant_id is rejected outright, tenant_id is derived solely from TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix).

INV-2, INV-3, INV-5 -- NOT-APPLICABLE (S4/S5 not started; no API route or lookup-by-ID endpoint added by this diff -- confirmed via git diff --stat ec8766d2..HEAD, zero router/controller/web/ files touched).

INV-4 (secrets by reference) -- APPLIES (live invariant), SATISFIED / not touched. This diff resolves/reads no new secret material. grep -rn System.get_env across config/ and the diff's own files shows only pre-existing, unrelated env-var reads (DB port, Keycloak port, secrets master key, log level) -- none introduced by REQ-228. Heuristic hardcoded-secret grep against lib/letflow/entities/ and lib/letflow/event_store.ex: zero hits.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove scoping) -- APPLIES, SATISFIED by this handoff itself (explicit statement of which invariants apply and how each is satisfied, as required).

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES, SATISFIED. grep -rn 'Repo.query' across lib/letflow/entities/, lib/letflow/event_store.ex, and both new migrations: zero hits. All access is via Ecto.Schema/Ecto.Query/Repo.insert/Repo.update/Repo.get -- parameterized by construction. Both migrations' own comments correctly note no tenant/user-controlled data is interpolated into SQL (prefix() is an Ecto-resolved trusted value, not caller input).

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES, SATISFIED. grep -n '^\s*{:ok, .*} = ' against every new/changed file in this diff: the two hits (event_store.ex:793, records.ex:360) are both inside `case`/pattern-match clauses handling already-narrowed values, not bare assignment-that-can-raise on external I/O -- not violations. Every path touching tenant input in Records/EntityTypeInstance/EventTypes uses `with`/`case` typed-result chains throughout.

INV-9 (SSRF/outbound URL) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No outbound HTTP call added by this diff.

Highest-risk item -- Letflow.EventStore.append_multi/3 refactor: read the full diff (git diff ec8766d2..HEAD -- lib/letflow/event_store.ex). append/2 and append_platform_event/2 are UNMODIFIED as functions; the only structural change is `defp build_multi(ctx), do: build_multi_composable(Multi.new(), ctx)` -- build_multi/1's own body was extracted verbatim into build_multi_composable/2 and is now called with Multi.new() for append/2's existing behavior (byte-identical) and with a caller-supplied open Multi for the new append_multi/3 path. No M1-M6 step logic, validation order, or transaction semantics changed. Independently ran: mix test test/letflow/event_store/ -> 150/150 passed; mix test test/letflow/entities/ -> 84/84 passed; mix test test/letflow/engine/ -> 977 passed (1 property, 976 tests), 16 excluded, 0 failures -- all three figures match the ELIXIR-DEV handoff's own claims exactly, confirming zero regression to the shared event-append core used by every other caller (including Engine.TaskActivation's own append_multi/6 usage). mix compile --warnings-as-errors: clean.

Idempotency-key handling: claim_idempotency/resolve_duplicate (event_store.ex ~line 648) is called with prefix: schema_name throughout -- the event_idempotency table is itself schema-per-tenant (confirmed same `if prefix()` migration pattern used across the codebase, pre-existing and unmodified by this diff), so idempotency_key uniqueness is enforced within one tenant's own Postgres schema, not a shared cross-tenant table -- no cross-tenant collision is possible regardless of key content. Duplicate-resubmission record reconstruction (Records.duplicate_result/1) decodes only the ORIGINAL EVENT's own stored payload (already tenant/schema-scoped by the query that fetched it) -- cannot return another tenant's or another entity's record.

The 4 flagged discrepancies, reviewed for security implications: (a) entity_type_instance_guard as an eager pre-Multi call (EntityTypeInstance.get_or_create/2) instead of a lazy Multi step -- no TOCTOU risk: get_or_create/2's own protocol is insert-with-on_conflict::nothing (conflict_target: :entity_type) followed by re-SELECT of whichever row actually won the race, the same idiom EventStore's own assign_sequence/3 and claim_idempotency/3 already use for exactly this reason -- concurrent first-creation of the same entity_type cannot produce two rows (the primary key enforces this at the DB level) and always converges on one winner's instance_id. No bypass of the exactly-one-row guarantee. (b) entity_def_version's string (hex-encoded binary) vs integer type in the outer JSON envelope: no injection/validation-bypass risk -- it is validated as `{"type": "string"}` by the outer envelope schema (Registry.validate_payload/3) and independently round-tripped via Base.encode16/decode16! with case: :lower, a fixed-alphabet, fully self-validating encoding (Base.decode16! raises rather than silently accepting malformed input) -- this is a data-shape fix, not a validation weakening. (c) definition_document/1's string-to-atom conversion: bounded and safe -- String.to_existing_atom/1 is used (not String.to_atom/1), so it can only ever produce an atom from Letflow's own closed, already-compiled field-type atom set (Definition.Validator/Record.Validator's own atoms); a malformed/attacker-controlled 'type' string that isn't already a known atom raises ArgumentError rather than silently producing a wrong-but-valid-looking atom-keyed map -- this is a fail-closed conversion, not a fail-open one. (d) removed redundant unique_index on entity_type_instances.entity_type: confirmed the table's primary key IS entity_type itself (`add :entity_type, :string, size: 255, primary_key: true`, migration line 25) -- the primary key alone already enforces global (per-tenant-schema) uniqueness on that column with no gap; EntityTypeInstance.insert_changeset/2's unique_constraint(:entity_type, name: :entity_type_instances_pkey) correctly targets the PK's own index. No uniqueness gap introduced.

Validation-before-write ordering (INV-8/correctness): confirmed in records.ex -- fetch_active_definition/2 and validate_field_values/2 (REQ-227's inner check) both run inside the outer `with` chain in create_record/2, update_record/2, update_record/2 BEFORE run_command/2 is ever called, i.e. before any Ecto.Multi exists (records.ex lines 135-136, 170-173, 201-202). EventStore.append_multi/3's own outer-envelope Registry.validate_payload/3 check (event_store.ex line 228) runs inside its own `with` chain before `build_multi_composable/2` is invoked -- 'multi left completely untouched, zero DB writes attempted' on any validation failure, matching append/2's existing documented discipline. No race between validation and the event append: both checks are synchronous, pre-transaction, sequential Elixir code.

No SQL injection: confirmed (INV-7 section above). No route/controller/web file added: confirmed via git diff --stat (18 files changed, all under lib/letflow/, priv/repo/migrations/, test/, handoffs/, lib/letflow/design/ -- zero router/controller/web/ hits).

Verdict: PASS. No BLOCKER findings on any applicable invariant. Routing to REVIEWER per WF-02 Step 2c.
